Can You Dispute Hard Inquiries Yourself? Yes. Here's the Honest Truth About Why Most People Hit a Wall.

You can file hard inquiry disputes on your own. The Federal Trade Commission provides tools, and nothing stops you from writing to the bureaus directly. We believe in being transparent about that.

Here's what typically happens: you send a dispute, and the bureau responds within 30 days. They either say the inquiry was "verified" — which sounds final but isn't — or they delete it. The challenge is that "verified" is not the same as "authorized." Bureaus verify that the pull happened. They do not verify that you gave permissible purpose. That legal distinction is where most self-filers give up, and where we begin.

The other reality is the knowledge gap. Knowing which specific provision of the FCRA applies to a dealership's shotgun credit pull is different from knowing which provision of the FDCPA applies to a debt collector pulling your report without permissible purpose. Applying Metro 2 compliance arguments requires knowing how furnishers are required to report and what happens when they don't follow the standard. These are not things you pick up in an afternoon of research — they are the only thing we have spent 11 years doing.

What you can do on your own:

  • File a basic dispute with each bureau
  • Request your free annual credit reports
  • Flag an inquiry as potentially unauthorized

What we do that changes the outcome:

  • Build legally precise, individualized dispute letters that bureaus cannot dismiss as boilerplate
  • Apply the correct federal statute to each specific inquiry type
  • Follow up strategically when a bureau responds with "verified" rather than accepting it as final
  • Handle every communication so nothing falls through the cracks
  • Move as fast as the law allows because we know your goals are on a timeline

If you have already tried on your own and hit a wall, that is the most common story we hear. It isn't a reflection on you — it's a reflection on how specialized this process actually is.

Choose Your Bureau — Each One Has Its Own Dispute Process and Its Own Pitfalls

Equifax , Experian , and TransUnion handle hard inquiry disputes differently. Different mailing addresses. Different escalation paths. Different reasons disputes fail. Pick the bureau that's blocking you and get the bureau-specific playbook.

Bureau

Experian

Experian's online disputes get auto-processed in days with boilerplate "verified" responses. Custom letters citing the right FCRA provisions trigger an actual reinvestigation — and that's where removal happens.

Experian inquiry removal →
Bureau

TransUnion

Credit Karma's Direct Dispute tool sends real TransUnion disputes — and they almost always come back "verified." A 15 U.S.C. § 1681b permissible-purpose challenge is a different question entirely.

TransUnion inquiry removal →
Bureau

Equifax

CFPB ordered Equifax to pay $15M in 2025 for improperly investigating disputes. A "verified" response from Equifax is not the end of the road — it's often where the actual escalation begins.

Equifax inquiry removal →
